subject: SIG: identity & access controls — SSO/SCIM/RBAC/MFA details
messages:

Cc: Kristin Park <kristin.park@acmecorp.com>, Acme Security <security@acmecorp.com>

Subject: SIG follow-up — identity controls (SSO/SCIM/RBAC/MFA)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team is working through the SIG questionnaire and flagged a few follow-ups specifically around identity and access controls. Could you provide concrete answers and evidence for the items below?

1) SSO/SAML: Does Redwood support SAML 2.0 IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows? Can you provide SAML metadata and an example assertion?
2) SCIM: Is SCIM 2.0 supported for provisioning? What attributes are synced, and what is the SCIM schema?
3) RBAC: Where can we find the role matrix and which admin roles can invite / provision users?
4) MFA & enforcement: Is MFA enforced for all staff and for admin users? Any exceptions?
5) Least privilege: How do you enforce least-privilege on service accounts and API keys?

We are aiming to complete the SIG by EOD Tuesday (6/16). If you can send the answers and any artifacts (metadata, screenshots, RBAC export), that would be great.

Thanks,
Tom Brewer
Sr. Security Engineer, Acme Corp

--
Acme Security (security@acmecorp.com)

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — identity controls (SSO/SCIM/RBAC/MFA)

Tom —

Appreciate the clarity on scope. I'm looping in Marissa (security lead) and Dev (infra) to provide the detailed technical responses and artifacts. We'll assemble a single SIG response workbook + supporting files and send back by EOD today (we should make that deadline).

High-level answers up front:
- SSO: We support SAML 2.0 (IdP/SP, both flows) and OIDC.
- SCIM: SCIM 2.0 push provisioning is supported with attribute mapping and deprovisioning.
- RBAC: Role-based model with pre-defined roles (Viewer, Developer, Operator, Admin) and custom role support in Dedicated/Private deployments.
- MFA: MFA is enforced for all interactive Redwood console users; admin roles require MFA.
- Least privilege: API keys are scoped and time-boxed; service principals follow ACLs and are rotatable via our secrets workflow.

We'll attach the SAML metadata, SCIM schema diagram, and an RBAC matrix for your review. If you need a redacted assertion example or a short screen recording of provisioning via SCIM, let us know.

Thanks — sending artifacts shortly.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — identity controls (SSO/SCIM/RBAC/MFA)

Folks — attaching the technical artifacts requested. Quick notes per item (copying the language we usually use in SIG responses):

1) SSO / SAML
- Supported: SAML 2.0 (SP-initiated and IdP-initiated).
- Metadata: attached saml-metadata.xml (SP metadata).
- Assertions: we can provide a redacted example assertion on request; we do not publish live assertions.
- Encryption/Signing: Assertions can be signed; we support both HTTP-POST and HTTP-Redirect bindings.

2) SCIM
- Supported: SCIM 2.0 for user provisioning (push).
- Default attribute set: userName, externalId, name (givenName, familyName), emails, active, groups.
- Deprovisioning: 'active' set to false triggers deprovisioning and disables session tokens.
- Attached: scim-schema.png (mapping diagram).

3) RBAC
- Roles: Viewer (read-only), Developer (deploy/read), Operator (manage runtime), Admin (org-level config).
- Admin scope: Admins can invite users, create service principals. Tenant-level owners exist for Dedicated/Private.
- Attached: rbac-matrix.csv (export of role -> permissions).

4) MFA & enforcement
- Enforcement: MFA (TOTP + FIDO2 options) is enforced for all console access. Admin and security-related roles are forced to use MFA via policy.
- Exceptions: Machine-to-machine integrations use scoped API keys or service principals (see least-privilege notes).

5) Least privilege
- API keys: support scoped keys (read-only, embed-only, inference-only) with expiration and rotation endpoints.
- Service principals: scoped to specific projects; require key rotation every 90 days per default policy; we can set stricter policies on Dedicated deployments.

Artifacts attached (zipped in the SIG workbook): saml-metadata.xml, scim-schema.png, rbac-matrix.csv. If Acme needs an exporter in CSV with account IDs redacted, say the word and I will produce that.

– Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: saml-metadata.xml (application/xml), scim-schema.png (image/png), rbac-matrix.csv (text/csv)

Thanks team — good first pass. A couple of compliance notes before we share externally:

- Redact internal account IDs from rbac-matrix.csv and replace with role placeholders (we should not expose internal tenant UUIDs).
- For SAML, include only the SP metadata (ok), and offer a redacted assertion example rather than a real one.
- For SCIM schema, add a short footnote explaining sync frequency and conflict resolution (we use last-write wins with timestamped updates).
- Add a one-page control narrative mapping key SIG questions to our SOC 2 controls (I started a draft in the SIG workbook).

I'm attaching a consolidated workbook (redwood-sig-response-20260615.xlsx) that combines answers, evidence references, and a column for "evidence provided" with filenames. Please use this as the single artifact we send to Acme.

I'll also request that the artifacts be uploaded to the secure shared Drive link (see link above) rather than sending attachments over email if Acme prefers.

Laura Bennett
